newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SCMP sees "rewarding" year ahead.
newsitem.headline: SCMP sees "rewarding" year ahead.

text.p: South China Morning Post (Holdings) Ltd, which posted a 20 percent increase in 1995/96 net profit due to a hefty exceptional item, painted a rosy picture for the year ahead citing an improved economy.

"We expect an improvement in the Hong Kong economy in the coming year largely due to positive signs in the retail and property market, a lower unemployment figure, and an anticipated increase of visitors to Hong Kong," company said.

Together with an expected drop in newsprint costs and improved results from its new subsidiary TVE (Holdings) Ltd, that would provide for a "rewarding year ahead", the newspaper publisher said in its results statement.
The company saw its net profit jump to HK$695.87 million in 1995/96 from HK$580.06 in 1994/95. Earnings per share rose to 44.90 cents versus 38.67 cents.
But the jump was more than accounted for by an exceptional item of HK$181 million gained from the disposal of the group's old headquarters building at Quarry Bay.

Prior to exceptionals and contribution from associates, operating profit fell to HK$602.34 million from HK$692.71 million, while earnings per share would have only been at 33.22 cents, the statement said. -- HONG KONG NEWSROOM (852)2843-6441
